critical_code_review_comments: rides.py:114 _is_scheduled_pending_activation checks ride.get('ride_mode') but create_ride stores the value under key 'mode' (rides.py:751). The function still works because of the fallback on scheduled_at, but the ride_mode key check is effectively dead code — consider standardising on 'mode'.
rides.py:1700 driver_cancel_booking similarly checks ride.get('ride_mode') == 'scheduled' (key never set); behaviour is rescued by `bool(ride.get('scheduled_at'))`. Same naming inconsistency.
rides.py is 2521 lines long — consider further splitting (driver/accept module, active/current+expire module) for maintainability (>700 line guideline).

/rides/active/current returns the bare ride dict when active, but {'active_ride': null} when not — inconsistent response shape may complicate frontend typing. Suggest always wrapping in {active_ride: ride|null}.

_driver_schedule_conflict treats every existing engagement without scheduled_at as an in-progress instant ride (good), but accepted-then-not-yet-started instant rides are also captured — confirm Phase-4 'pre-book next' is still possible since the same /accept endpoint is reused (the code comment notes this; tests should add a regression for it).
